items: Document Your Damages: List every category of money owed, including rent shortfalls, utilities, shared household expenses, and any repairs you covered that were her responsibility.
Document Your Damages: Assign specific dollar amounts to each line item and calculate your total by multiplying recurring expenses by the number of months she failed to pay.
Document Your Damages: Categorize each claim by documentation strength as documentable, partially documentable, or estimate-only, so you know exactly which items will hold up in court.
Document Your Damages: Verify your state's statute of limitations to confirm all claims fall within the legal time window before you invest time and money in this process.
Build Your Evidence File: Collect all receipts, bank statements, and transaction records that support each documentable and partially documentable claim you plan to file.
Build Your Evidence File: Gather any written agreements, text messages, or emails where she acknowledged owing money or agreed to specific payment arrangements.
Build Your Evidence File: Compile payment app history and written communications that show a pattern of late, missing, or incomplete payments from her to you.
Build Your Evidence File: Organize your complete evidence file chronologically with clear labels so you can quickly locate any document during your hearing.
Start the Legal Process: Send a formal demand letter that creates a legal record and starts the official response clock required before filing in small claims court.
Start the Legal Process: File your claim in the correct small claims court jurisdiction, which is typically where she currently resides or where your rental agreement was signed.
Start the Legal Process: Present your itemized claims with organized documentation during the hearing, showing each amount owed alongside its supporting evidence for the judge.
Start the Legal Process: Develop an enforcement strategy for your judgment, since having a court order doesn't guarantee automatic payment and you may need to pursue wage garnishment or bank levies.
